## F1

Spec and documentation: RFC 8949 §5.5: “different language environments pose different restrictions on the range and precision of numbers that are representable.” Crate `ValueImpl::Negative` doc: “Only 63 bits of information are used here.”

Minimal example (escaped): `\x3b\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff`. Hex: `3bffffffffffffffff`.

Expected: A range error for a value outside the declared model.

Actual: OutOfRangeIntegerValue.

Reproduce: `./run_all.sh`, then inspect [minimal-repros.json](evidence/gen/minimal-repros.json), the applicable vector row, and the named mutant probe.

Known-item check: M003 probe; Appendix A vector 12 is not applicable. No matching unresolved issue was found in the supplied issue titles.

Confidence: high for the observed bounded behaviour; the documented profile interpretation is limited as stated.

## F2

Spec and documentation: RFC 8949 §5.5: “For an integer-only application, a protocol may want to completely exclude the use of floating-point values.” The public error variants are `UnsupportedFloatingPointValue` and `UnsupportedSimpleValue`.

Minimal example (escaped): `\xf9\x3e\x00 / \xf0`. Hex: `f93e00 / f0`.

Expected: Errors for unsupported forms.

Actual: UnsupportedFloatingPointValue / UnsupportedSimpleValue.

Reproduce: `./run_all.sh`, then inspect [minimal-repros.json](evidence/gen/minimal-repros.json), the applicable vector row, and the named mutant probe.

Confidence: high for the observed bounded behaviour; the documented profile interpretation is limited as stated.

## F3

Spec and documentation: Crate `read` and `write` docs: “Maximum level of nesting supported is 127”. RFC 8949 §5 permits application subsets.

Minimal example (escaped): `127 copies of \x81 then \x00; one more array exceeds the default budget`. Hex: `81 repeated 127 times, then 00`.

Expected: 127 arrays succeed; 128 fail. Explicit None permits tested deeper values.

Actual: Both default boundaries match; new tests expose shipped-suite omissions.

Reproduce: `./run_all.sh`, then inspect [minimal-repros.json](evidence/gen/minimal-repros.json), the applicable vector row, and the named mutant probe.

Known-item check: The supplied #373 change establishes the default limit. M021/M035 check its exact boundary.

Confidence: high for the observed bounded behaviour; the documented profile interpretation is limited as stated.

## F4

Spec and documentation: Crate `Value::map` docs: “You may not call this function with identical keys in its argument.” RFC 8949 §5.3.2 permits forwarding tags without converting their content to native semantic types.

Minimal example (escaped): `\xa2\x00\x00\x00\x01 / \xc0\x00`. Hex: `a200000001 / c000`.

Expected: Duplicate encoded keys cause an error; constructing duplicate Value keys panics. The codec preserves an uninterpreted tag.

Actual: OutOfOrderKey; documented constructor panic; tag(0,unsigned(0)) is preserved.

Reproduce: `./run_all.sh`, then inspect [minimal-repros.json](evidence/gen/minimal-repros.json), the applicable vector row, and the named mutant probe.

Known-item check: #639 moved duplicate rejection into construction. CTAP tag prohibition belongs to the message layer, excluded here.

Confidence: high for the observed bounded behaviour; the documented profile interpretation is limited as stated.

## F5

Spec and documentation: RFC 8949 §4.2.1: “Indefinite-length items MUST NOT appear.” Reader docs only say “Deserialize CBOR binary data to produce a single Value”.

Confidence: high for the observed bounded behaviour; the documented profile interpretation is limited as stated.

## F6

Spec and documentation: Crate README: “Serialized version is in canonical order.” RFC 8949 §4.2.1 requires “bytewise lexicographic order”. RFC 7049 §3.9 says “If two keys have different lengths, the shorter one sorts earlier”. CTAP 2.1 §8 says “If the major types are different, the one with the lower value in numerical order sorts earlier.”

Minimal example (escaped): `\xa2\x18\x18\x00\x20\x00`. Hex: `a21818002000`.

Expected: RFC 8949 and CTAP scalar order place unsigned 24 before negative -1; RFC 7049 length-first places -1 first.

Actual: The crate writes and accepts a21818002000, and rejects a22000181800 as OutOfOrderKey.

Reproduce: `./run_all.sh`, then inspect [minimal-repros.json](evidence/gen/minimal-repros.json), the applicable vector row, and the named mutant probe.

Known-item check: Arrays/maps/tags sort like encoded bytes, but CTAP excludes such keys from its scalar-key comparison note.

Confidence: high for the observed bounded behaviour; the documented profile interpretation is limited as stated.

## F7

Spec and documentation: Crate `cbor_map_options` docs: “Duplicate keys will lead to invalid CBOR, i.e. writing these values fails.” `Value::map` instead documents a construction panic. The `write_nested` docs link `DecoderError::TooMuchNesting`, but the function returns `EncoderError`.

Minimal example (escaped): `API expression cbor_map_options! { 0 => 1, 0 => 2 }; rustdoc for write_nested`. Hex: `No wire output exists before construction fails.`.

Expected: The macro documentation should describe the construction panic. The write_nested nesting-error link should resolve to EncoderError::TooMuchNesting.

Actual: Construction panics; EncoderError::DuplicateMapKey has no reachable public branch. Rustdoc warns that DecoderError::TooMuchNesting is an unresolved link in writer.rs:36.

Reproduce: `./run_all.sh`, then inspect [minimal-repros.json](evidence/gen/minimal-repros.json), the applicable vector row, and the named mutant probe.

Known-item check: #639 removed the old writer duplicate tests and moved duplicate rejection into Value::map. The remaining macro prose is stale. The separate upstream-doc.patch corrects both documentation defects without code changes. No normative wire deviation is claimed.

Confidence: high for the observed bounded behaviour; the documented profile interpretation is limited as stated.

## F8

Spec and documentation: RFC 8949 §3.1 major types 2/3: the argument counts the bytes of string content. #788 source comment: “Casting a u64 length to usize would silently truncate it on 32-bit platforms”.

Minimal example (escaped): `\x5b\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00`. Hex: `5b0000000100000000`.

Expected: Reject announced content that is not present.

Actual: IncompleteCborData for both byte and text forms.

Reproduce: `./run_all.sh`, then inspect [minimal-repros.json](evidence/gen/minimal-repros.json), the applicable vector row, and the named mutant probe.

Known-item check: KNOWN #788. The real cast regression is equivalent on this host; explicit u32 truncation models the old 32-bit behaviour and is detected by shipped tests. Native 32-bit execution remains a gap.

Confidence: high for the observed bounded behaviour; the documented profile interpretation is limited as stated.

## Checked with no deviation

Major types 0–7 within the declared model; additional arguments 24–27; reserved 28–30 and indefinite marker 31 rejection; preferred integer/length/tag widths; text UTF-8; scalar and complex map-key order; duplicate rejection; truncation; trailing data; depth budgets; tags; unsupported simple/float errors; writer append and write/read round trips.

The independent reference comparison used seed 8949, 1094 generated values and 363057 unique byte inputs. 149157 succeeded and 213900 returned errors. Acceptance/rejection agreed for every input. Exact round-trip bytes and independent decoded structures agreed for every accepted input. No native panic or hang occurred. Every one- and two-byte input was included. Longer cases used generated values, truncations, insertion/deletion/substitution variants, boundary strings and fixed-seed random bytes. Full split-stream equivalence is not applicable because no streaming API exists.

The public `read_nested(..., None)` escape hatch is only tested at bounded depths. Arbitrarily deep recursion and memory exhaustion are not covered by this finite run. The existing fuzz target checks accepted decode/write byte identity; the independent comparison does not depend on that target or its corpus.
